<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Mr.&#160;Peng retired from AMD in August 2024. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc869673_26">Executive Summary </p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">2024 Business Highlights </span></p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">AMD delivered record revenue of $25.8&#160;billion in fiscal 2024, up 14&#160;percent compared to last year, as strong growth in our Data Center and Client segments more than offset headwinds in our Gaming and Embedded segments. Data Center segment annual revenue of $12.6&#160;billion increased 94% compared to the prior year driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> and AMD EPYC<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> processors. Data Center segment annual revenue nearly doubled and contributed approximately 50% of total annual revenue. Client segment revenue of $7.1&#160;billion, up 52% compared to the prior year, was driven by higher sales of AMD Ryzen<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> mobile and desktop processors. Gaming segment revenue declined 58% from the prior year to $2.6&#160;billion primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue. Embedded segment revenue declined 33% from the prior year to $3.6&#160;billion primarily due to customers normalizing their inventory levels. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Gross margin for the year was 49%, compared to 46% last year, driven primarily by a favorable shift in revenue mix based on higher Data Center and Client revenues and lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by negative impact of lower Embedded revenue. Operating income was $1.9&#160;billion, compared to operating income of $401&#160;million for fiscal 2023, primarily driven by higher revenue, partially offset by increased R&amp;D investments. Net income was $1.6&#160;billion, compared to $854&#160;million in the prior year, primarily driven by higher revenue. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">During the year, we successfully launched multiple leadership products and made significant progress executing our AI strategy. One of our priorities in 2024 was to accelerate growth in our Data Center segment. The demand for our Data Center AI accelerator products was very strong led by production deployments by AMD Instinct MI300X GPU accelerators by large hyperscale cloud customers. To further expand our high-performance server CPU portfolio, we launched our 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors, formerly codenamed &#8220;Turin,&#8221; built with our latest &#8220;Zen 5&#8221; core architecture designed to deliver leadership performance and efficiency. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We took a major step in our AI PC roadmap with the launch of AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series processors that combine leadership compute capabilities based on our &#8220;Zen 5&#8221; architecture and an industry-leading neural processing unit (&#8220;NPU&#8221;) powered by our XDNA 2 architecture for next-generation AI PCs. We added to our Ryzen family of desktop CPUs with the Ryzen 9000 series processors for laptop and desktop PCs that deliver leadership performance in gaming, productivity and content creation. We extended our multigenerational partnership with Sony as they introduced the PlayStation<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> 5 Pro, which features a new AMD semi-custom SoC that delivers increased graphics and ray tracing performance and enables <span style="white-space:nowrap">AI-driven</span> upscaling. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#8194;2025 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#8194;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis</span> (continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">end-to-end</span></span> acceleration of <span style="white-space:nowrap">AI-driven</span> embedded systems. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams across AMD to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning our full product portfolio. We made several key optimizations and introduced new features in the latest AMD ROCm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">TM</sup> software that increased performance in key generative AI workloads, expanded support for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplified the overall developer experience. We also made strategic investments to further expand our AI software capabilities with the acquisition of Silo AI Oy (&#8220;Silo AI&#8221;), an AI lab based in Finland that enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware. Silo AI has also developed a software stack used to train multiple <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">state-of-the-art</span></span></span> large language models (&#8220;LLMs&#8221;) on AMD Instinct accelerators that can accelerate the development of highly-performant AMD training solutions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August to acquire ZT Group Int&#8217;l, Inc. (&#8220;ZT Systems&#8221;), a provider of AI and general-purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies. We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of fiscal year 2025, subject to certain regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. We intend to seek a strategic partner to acquire ZT Systems&#8217; manufacturing business. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our balance sheet remained strong with cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of December&#160;28, 2024 at $5.1&#160;billion, compared to $5.8&#160;billion at the end of December&#160;30, 2023. Our aggregate principal amount of total debt as of December&#160;28, 2024 was $1.8&#160;billion, compared to $2.5&#160;billion as of December&#160;30, 2023. We repaid our 2.95% Senior Notes due 2024 with a principal amount of $750&#160;million in June 2024. During the year, we repurchased 5.9&#160;million shares under our stock repurchase program, returning $862&#160;million to stockholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We ended the year with significant momentum, reflected by record revenue for both the fourth quarter and for the full year and CPU market share gains that accelerated throughout 2024. We also successfully established our multi-billion-dollar Data Center AI business and accelerated both our AMD Instinct hardware and AMD ROCm software roadmaps to address significant AI market opportunities. </p>

 </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">2024 Executive Compensation Program &#8211; Highlights </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Overview </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We operate in a challenging, highly competitive and rapidly evolving global business environment. It is critical that we retain and motivate a talented and experienced executive team. Accordingly, our Compensation Committee has implemented and oversees an executive compensation program that emphasizes pay for performance, advances our business strategies and objectives, drives the creation of long-term sustainable stockholder value, and attracts, retains and motivates a high-caliber executive team. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For fiscal 2024, the vast majority of our Named Executive Officers&#8217; compensation continued to be delivered through long-term equity awards. The performance-based restricted stock unit (&#8220;PRSU&#8221;) awards that vested in 2024 reflected our exceptional stock price performance for the three-year period from August&#160;9, 2021 through August&#160;9, 2024, relative to the total shareholder return of the S&amp;P 500. Our total shareholder return of 79.99% for this three-year performance period was 53.54% higher than the total shareholder return of the S&amp;P 500 during the same period. As a result, each of our Named Executive Officers (other than Ms.&#160;Hu, Ms.&#160;Hahn and Mr.&#160;Peng, who were not employed by us during 2021) vested in 200% of the target number of PRSUs covered by their fiscal 2021 annual PRSU awards. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Each of our Named Executive Officers (other than Mr.&#160;Peng) also received a cash incentive award under our Executive Incentive Plan (&#8220;EIP&#8221;) for fiscal 2024 based on the achievement of revenue, adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income and adjusted free cash flow performance goals and the achievement of key strategic milestones. Despite our achievements, we did not meet our aggressive internal financial targets which are intentionally set to be rigorous and challenging to align with our pay for performance philosophy, resulting in below target payouts under the EIP. Based on this performance, our Named Executive Officers received a payout under the EIP for fiscal 2024 of 72.2% of target. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">2024 Executive Compensation Program &#8211; Emphasis on &#8220;Pay for Performance&#8221; </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As illustrated below, the target total direct compensation (defined below) of our Named Executive Officers (other than Mr.&#160;Peng) in 2024 was weighted heavily towards performance-based compensation: </p> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

She also received a long-term equity incentive award for the 2024 fiscal year with a target value of $3.5&#160;million subject to similar vesting and other terms and conditions as the annual long-term incentive awards granted to our other executive team members in August 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Ms.&#160;Hahn also received a <span style="white-space:nowrap">sign-on</span> equity award of (a)&#160;a target number of PRSUs having an aggregate intended target value of $1.5&#160;million (or a target number of 9,071 PRSUs) and (b)&#160;time-based RSUs having an intended target value of $1.5&#160;million (or 9,071 time-based RSUs). The time-based RSUs vest in four equal annual installments beginning on February&#160;15, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Ms. Hahn&#8217;s &#8220;make whole&#8221; compensation was designed to be economically equivalent to the equity compensation opportunities she forfeited upon her departure from her prior employer. It was comprised of (a) time-based restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) having an aggregate intended target value of $6 million (36,284 time-based RSUs) that are scheduled to vest (i) 6,047 on September 15, 2024, (ii) 12,095 on January 15, 2025, and (iii) 18,142 on January&#160;15, 2026, generally subject to her continued service through the applicable vesting date and (b) a sign-on cash bonus of $2 million. Ms.&#160;Hahn is required to repay the <span style="white-space:nowrap">sign-on</span> cash bonus in full if her employment terminates within the first thirteen months following her start date, or, if her employment terminates after thirteen months and before the 24th month following her start date, her repayment obligation is prorated based on each full month of employment following her thirteenth month of employment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Ms.&#160;Hahn&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">sign-on</span> and make-whole equity awards are subject to the terms and conditions of the 2023 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2023 Plan&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc869673_27">Response to 2024 &#8220;Say On Pay&#8221; Vote and Stockholder Engagement Process </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee seeks to align the objectives of our executive compensation program with the interests of our stockholders. When evaluating our executive compensation program, the Compensation Committee carefully considers both the results of our annual advisory resolution on the compensation of our Named Executive Officers (the &#8220;say on pay&#8221; proposal) as well as direct feedback from our stockholders, with whom we actively and directly engage throughout the fiscal year. At our 2024 annual meeting of stockholders, our &#8220;say on pay&#8221; proposal received support from approximately 80% of the votes cast on the proposal, reflecting widespread stockholder support for our fiscal 2024 executive compensation program. As in prior years, we were mindful of the strong support our stockholders expressed for our program as we evaluated our compensation practices for fiscal 2024. Upon completion of our evaluation, we decided to retain the overall design of our executive compensation program. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">During fiscal 2024, we continued our practice of proactive stockholder engagement regarding executive compensation, environmental, social and governance (&#8220;ESG&#8221;), and other corporate governance matters. We do not rely solely on the proxy season as our active stockholder engagement season, instead we prefer to actively and directly engage with stockholders throughout the fiscal year. After filing and disseminating our definitive proxy statement for our 2024 annual meeting of stockholders, we conducted conference calls, <span style="white-space:nowrap">in-person</span> and virtual meetings, or other types of engagements with several of our top 100 institutional stockholders (and approximately 60% of the shares of common stock entitled to vote at our annual meeting) to solicit feedback on AMD, including their views on our executive compensation structure and pay policies and practices. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In summary, stockholder feedback centered on the following themes: </p> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">In the aggregate, feedback received during these discussions continued to be supportive of our executive compensation program and our compensation program design, and we received feedback that AMD has a well-functioning incentive program which appropriately promotes and rewards strong long-term performance. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">We shared stockholder feedback with the Compensation Committee, which considers both the results of our <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">say-on-pay</span></span> vote as well as direct feedback from stockholders to align the objectives of our executive compensation program with the interests of our stockholders. As we evaluated our compensation practices for 2024, the Compensation Committee considered the support we received from our stockholders for the overall design of our executive compensation program during our 2024 engagement as well as in the past. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Further, we have not and will not enter into change of control agreements that provide cash change of control payments that exceed (i)&#160;two times the sum of base salary and target annual incentive bonus plus (ii)&#160;the <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</span> target annual incentive bonus for the year in which the termination of employment occurs.</td></tr>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc869673_29">Compensation Philosophy and Objectives </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Pay for Performance </span></p> <p style="margin-top:3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our executive compensation program philosophy centers on pay for performance and is guided by the following primary principles: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We continually assess and adjust our executive compensation program, policies and practices taking into account these guiding principles and based on feedback obtained through our stockholder engagement efforts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Talent Management Focus </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee places a strong emphasis on developing, motivating, retaining, and attracting talent that is critical to guide and execute our strategy as well as to continue to grow our business. Our executive compensation program aligns with our talent objectives and our compensation decisions not only consider individual and company performance, but also long-term potential, key retention goals and organizational succession plans. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As required by its charter, the Compensation Committee regularly reviews succession planning and talent development. The Compensation Committee at least annually reviews succession plans for the Chief Executive Officer and other senior executive positions. These reviews occur with input from our Chief Executive Officer, our Senior Vice President, Marketing, Communications and Human Resources, and our Senior Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer. The Compensation Committee also reviews succession plans in executive session, with no members of management present. Succession planning for key executive roles consists of an assessment of internal candidates and their development plans, as well as potential external talent, while factoring in our culture as well as diversity and belonging. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We believe that building a diverse talent pipeline, encouraging a culture of respect and belonging, and increasing inclusion of unique and underrepresented voices makes AMD stronger. In 2024, we continued to focus on developing our female engineering community through mentoring opportunities and expanding our &#8220;Advancing Women in Technology&#8221; program that aims to support career development. For additional information on our belonging and inclusion efforts, see our &#8220;Environmental, Social and Governance&#8221; section beginning on page 27. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Competitive Compensation </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We operate in a highly competitive business environment. We must offer market competitive compensation to recruit and retain top leadership and industry experts to guide and execute our business strategy. Accordingly, the Compensation Committee seeks to compensate our Named Executive Officers at competitive levels with compensation for executives in similar positions at identified peer companies (set forth below), which the Compensation Committee believes reflects the current competitive market for executive talent. The Compensation Committee, which consists of four independent directors, is responsible for reviewing our executive compensation program annually to evaluate its alignment with the strategies and needs of our business, market trends and the interests of our stockholders. The Compensation Committee is responsible for formulating compensation recommendations to the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-management</span><span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>members of our Board regarding our Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s compensation and for approving the compensation of our other Named Executive Officers.  <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Role of Compensation Consultant </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee has the authority to engage independent advisors to assist in carrying out its responsibilities. <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">the competitiveness of our executive compensation program by providing a market review of executive compensation and relevant trends, evaluating our compensation peer group composition and analyzing the compensation at our compensation peer group companies; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">the pay levels of our Named Executive Officers by assessing and advising on equity and cash compensation guidelines for various executive job levels and assessing compensation levels for our executive officers; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">our executive compensation program design, including short-term and long-term incentive plan design and pay mix, the framework for our long-term equity awards and our retention strategies, evaluation of our stock ownership guidelines, and assessment of severance and change of control arrangements; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">the compensation arrangements for the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-management</span> members of our Board. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Conflict of Interest Assessment for Compensation Consultant </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee recognizes the importance of receiving objective advice from its compensation consultant and conducts an annual conflicts of interest assessment of its compensation consultant. In 2024, Compensia did not provide any services to or receive any payments from us, except in its capacity as a consultant to the Compensation Committee. In March 2025, the Compensation Committee considered whether the services provided by Compensia raised any conflicts of interest pursuant to the rules of the SEC and the listing rules of Nasdaq and concluded that the work performed by Compensia did not raise any conflicts of interest. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In the course of its engagement, Compensia attended meetings of the Compensation Committee and, where applicable, presented its findings and recommendations for discussion. Compensia also consulted frequently with members of the Compensation Committee and met with members of senior management to obtain and validate market data, review materials, and discuss management&#8217;s compensation recommendations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Role of Management </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee is supported by our Chief Executive Officer (other than with respect to her own compensation) and other members of management. The Compensation Committee considers the input of these individuals to formulate the specific plan and award designs, including performance measures and performance levels, necessary to align our executive compensation program with our business objectives and strategies. These individuals did not attend either executive sessions or portions of any meetings of the Compensation Committee or our Board where their own compensation was discussed or determined. During the Compensation Committee&#8217;s annual review of executive compensation, our Chief Executive Officer reviews with the Compensation Committee her performance evaluations of each of our other Named Executive Officers and her compensation recommendations for those Named Executive Officers.&#8195; </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Competitive Pay Analysis </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Each year, the Compensation Committee reviews the compensation decisions of a custom group of peer companies in combination with industry-specific compensation survey data to develop an understanding of the &#8220;competitive market&#8221; with respect to current executive compensation levels and related policies and practices. The Compensation Committee then evaluates how our pay practices and our Named Executive Officers&#8217; compensation levels compared to the competitive market. As part of this evaluation, the Compensation Committee also reviews the performance measures and related performance target levels generally used within the competitive market to reward performance. The Compensation Committee believes that it appropriately sets the compensation of our Named Executive Officers, while taking into account the practices of our peers and industry best practices. </p>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#8194;2025 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#8194;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Discussion and Analysis</span> (continued)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span></p> <p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Methodology Used to Perform the Competitive Pay Analysis </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To assist the Compensation Committee in its review of the 2024 compensation for our Named Executive Officers, Compensia provided a competitive pay analysis in February 2024 that set forth compensation data developed from publicly available information, as of December 2023, of the companies included in a custom peer group (the &#8220;2024 Executive Compensation Peer Group&#8221;). In May 2024, Compensia provided the Compensation Committee an updated competitive pay analysis that reflected AMD&#8217;s and peer group financial data as of April&#160;24, 2024, and updated AMD&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-day</span> average stock price as of that date. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">To develop the 2024 Executive Compensation Peer Group, the Compensation Committee reviewed the group of companies comprising the then-existing compensation peer group in November 2023, with particular reference to their industry (i.e., business segment and key competitors), revenues (generally 50% to 200% of our revenues for the trailing four fiscal quarters) and market capitalization (generally 30% to 300% of our market capitalization), in each case based on then publicly available information. The Compensation Committee selected these latter two metrics because, based on Compensia&#8217;s analysis and holding all other factors constant, revenue has the greatest correlation to cash compensation levels and market capitalization has the greatest influence on equity compensation levels. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on this review, the Compensation Committee removed L3Harris Technologies, Inc., Microchip Technology Incorporated and Motorola Solutions, Inc. because they were below the target range for market capitalization, and, in the case of Microchip Technology Incorporated and Motorola Solutions, Inc., also below the target range for revenue. The Compensation Committee also removed KLA Corporation because it was below the target range for revenue and at the lower end of the target range for market capitalization. Based on this review, and in order to improve the statistical sampling of the peer group, the Compensation Committee added International Business Machines Corporation and SAP SA, each of which fit within the applicable criteria and is included in competitive benchmark sets for other high profile semiconductor companies. The Compensation Committee believes that the composition of the 2024 Executive Compensation Peer Group reflects an appropriate set of comparator companies for purposes of assessing our executive compensation program. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The companies comprising the 2024 Executive Compensation Peer Group are as follows: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(1)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Ms.&#160;Hahn joined AMD in January 2024. For a discussion of Ms.&#160;Hahn&#8217;s offer letter, see &#8220;&#8212;2024 General Counsel New Hire Package&#8221;. </p></td></tr></table>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(2)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Mr.&#160;Peng retired from AMD in August 2024. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Annual Cash Performance Bonuses </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Generally, short-term incentives in the form of an annual cash performance bonus are provided to our Named Executive Officers under the EIP. These bonuses are designed to reward short-term performance and the achievement of the principal goals of our annual operating plan. Each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s target bonus opportunity is a percentage of their base salary and is determined based on the competitive pay analysis conducted by the Compensation Committee as described above. For fiscal 2024, the target bonus opportunity was 200% of base salary for our CEO, which was unchanged from fiscal 2023, and 125% of base salary for the other Named Executive Officers (other than Ms.&#160;Hahn), which was unchanged from fiscal 2023. Mr.&#160;Peng retired from AMD in August 2024 and did not receive a bonus under the EIP for fiscal 2024. Ms.&#160;Hahn joined AMD on January&#160;15, 2024, and her target bonus opportunity under the EIP for fiscal 2024 was set at 100% of base salary pursuant to the terms of her individually negotiated offer letter. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the fiscal 2024 EIP, the amount of the annual cash performance bonus for each Named Executive Officer, other than Mr.&#160;Peng, was calculated based on (i)&#160;his or her target bonus opportunity, (ii)&#160;our corporate financial performance (weighted 80%) for fiscal 2024, as measured against <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</span> performance levels (the &#8220;Financial Performance Targets&#8221;) for the first half of fiscal 2024 (weighted 40%) and the second half of fiscal 2024 (weighted 60%), and (iii)&#160;achievement of strategic milestones (weighted 20%) established with respect to key engineering, business, commercial/operational, and sales and culture metrics (the &#8220;Strategic Milestones&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Financial Performance Targets for the first half of fiscal 2024 and the Strategic Milestones were approved by the Compensation Committee in February 2024. The Financial Performance Targets for the second half of fiscal 2024 were approved by the Compensation Committee in August 2024. In addition to assessing achievement of the fiscal 2024 performance goals, the Compensation Committee also performs an annual qualitative assessment of each Named Executive Officer&#8217;s individual performance. This assessment results in determination of an individual performance factor for each named executive that can increase or decrease his or her final EIP payout. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Financial Performance Targets </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee used the following financial performance measures and weightings as the Financial Performance Targets for the fiscal 2024 EIP: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;width:50%;border:0;margin:0 auto">

<td style=" BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:4pt ;BORDER-RIGHT:2.00pt solid #ffffff; BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff; padding-right:2pt;vertical-align:bottom;text-align:center"><span style="color:#ffffff"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="color:#ffffff">&#8195;Weighting&#8195;</span></span></span></td></tr>

<td style="padding-bottom:3pt ;BORDER-BOTTOM:1.00pt solid #a5a5a5;vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.00em; text-indent:-1.00em; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">&#8194;Adjusted Free Cash Flow</p></td>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income as a performance measure because it is a fair measure of our profitability and a valid metric for comparison, which the Compensation Committee believes is directly tied to enhanced<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>stock price performance. The Compensation Committee assigned it a weight of 50% because it is a key short-term financial measure for the operation of our business and is a measure of significant importance to our stockholders. For purposes of the fiscal 2024 EIP, our &#8220;adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income&#8221; was calculated by adjusting our fiscal 2024 GAAP net income for <span style="white-space:nowrap">(i)&#160;non-GAAP</span> financial adjustments such as amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, stock-based compensation, acquisition-related and other costs, restructuring charges and provision for income taxes associated with these adjustments and (ii)&#160;amounts accrued for fiscal 2024 annual cash performance bonuses. The aggregate amount of these adjustments is $4.2&#160;billion. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The Compensation Committee chose GAAP net revenue as a performance measure because it reflects our <span style="white-space:nowrap">top-line</span> growth, which the Compensation Committee believes is a strong indicator of our long-term ability to increase profitability, cash flow and improve stock price performance. Finally, the Compensation Committee chose adjusted free cash flow as a performance measure because it believes effective cash management and cash generation are key components of our strategy and our annual operating plan, the successful execution of which should lower indebtedness, increase financial flexibility and ultimately drive improved company valuation and stock price performance. For purposes of our fiscal 2024 EIP, our &#8220;adjusted free cash flow&#8221; was calculated by adjusting our GAAP net cash provided by operating activities for (i)&#160;purchases of property and equipment and (ii)&#160;cash payments for fiscal 2023 bonuses which were paid in March and April 2024. The aggregate amount of these adjustments is ($400) million. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income and adjusted free cash flow differ from the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> financial results we report in our quarterly earnings release materials and should be viewed in addition to and not as a substitute for, or superior to, reported results prepared in accordance with GAAP. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The following illustrates how the 2024 annual cash performance bonuses under the EIP were calculated: </p> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <div> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center">


<img src="g869673g08a08.jpg" alt="LOGO" style="width:6.67014in;height:2.30887in"/>

<img src="g869673g09a09.jpg" alt="LOGO" style="width:6.66493in;height:4.47851in"/>
 </p> </div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The performance levels (threshold, target and maximum)<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>for the first half and second half of fiscal 2024 financial performance measures were established by the Compensation Committee in February 2024 and August 2024, respectively, in each case in consultation with senior management. The performance levels were structured using our 2024 operating plan as a benchmark to align with our financial objectives for the fiscal periods, taking into account overall affordability of the bonus opportunities provided under the EIP for fiscal 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">These targets were determined by the Compensation Committee to be appropriately aggressive. The threshold and maximum levels for each financial measure was determined by the Compensation Committee to provide for appropriate payout above or below target. For each performance measure, the level of performance required increases at a fixed rate between each performance level. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Strategic Milestones </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For the Strategic Milestones, which account for 20% of the EIP Performance Factor (subject to possible adjustment as described above), the Compensation Committee selected (a)&#160;new product tape outs and launches tied to specified internal targeted delivery dates, (b)&#160;achievement of various commercial/operations milestones, and (c)&#160;workforce strategic objectives. Each of the specific Strategic Milestones is highly confidential information so we try to balance that with giving our stockholders transparency. Providing our specific milestones would give competitors a greater sense of our internal goals, milestones, strategy, and timelines. Disclosure would allow our competitors to adjust their own strategy in a way that would cause us irreparable competitive harm in the highly competitive semiconductor industry. When approved, the Compensation Committee believed that each Strategic Milestone was challenging, yet reasonably achievable. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on our performance relative to the Financial Performance Targets and Strategic Milestones, the fiscal 2024 EIP reached 72.2% achievement. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><span style="font-style:italic">Individual Performance Factor </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For fiscal 2024, the Compensation Committee reviewed individual performance based on achievement of objective measures and goals in the areas of execution, leadership, and innovation/strategic planning (the &#8220;Individual Performance Factor&#8221;). At the end of fiscal 2024, our Chief Executive Officer assessed each participating Named Executive Officer&#8217;s performance, except her own, and made bonus recommendations to the Compensation Committee for each of them. The Compensation Committee then considered the Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s individual performance reviews and bonus recommendations, and independently assessed the Company&#8217;s performance and the individual performance of the Chief Executive Officer and each of the other participating Named Executive Officers to determine the Individual Performance Factor. After consideration of the factors above, the Compensation Committee determined to award each participating Named Executive Officer an Individual Performance Factor of 1.0 to reflect the leadership and continued execution that contributed to the Company delivering strong performance across all businesses, including record annual revenue in 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Based on its assessment of each of these factors and considering the Company&#8217;s strong performance relative to our aggressive Financial Performance Targets and Strategic Milestones, the Compensation Committee approved fiscal 2024 annual cash performance bonuses under the EIP for the Named Executive Officers (other than Mr.&#160;Peng) as set forth below: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The stock options expire seven years after the grant date, subject to earlier expiration if the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s employment with us terminates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">RSUs</div></div>. For further information on this agreement, see the &#8220;Severance and Change in Control Arrangements&#8221; section beginning on page 74. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">With the exception of our Chief Executive Officer, each of our other Named Executive Officers is party to a change of control agreement with us. In addition, these agreements and the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">change-in-control</div></div> provisions in Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement are intended to provide incentives to the Named Executive Officer to effectively execute the directives of our Board, even in the event that such actions may result in the elimination of the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">AMD has a policy prohibiting it from entering into any new change of control agreements or arrangements containing an excise tax <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">gross-up</div> provision. Our Named Executive Officers&#8217; current change of control agreements and the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">change-of-control</div></div> provisions of Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement do not provide for excise tax <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">gross-ups.</div> </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: italic; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Termination of Employment Required to Trigger Payments </div></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Under the terms and conditions of these change of control agreements and the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">change-of-control</div></div> provisions of Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s employment agreement, each of our Named Executive Officers (other than Mr.&#160;Peng) is eligible to receive certain specified payments and benefits only if (a)&#160;a &#8220;change of control&#8221; of us occurs and (b)&#160;the Named Executive Officer&#8217;s employment is terminated or the Named Executive Officer is constructively discharged within two years of the change of control transaction (a &#8220;double trigger&#8221; arrangement). The Compensation Committee believes this structure strikes a balance between our incentive arrangements and our executive hiring and retention objectives without providing &#8220;windfall&#8221; payments and benefits to any Named Executive Officers who continue employment with an acquiring entity following a change of control of AMD. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">For a detailed description of these agreements and arrangements with our Named Executive Officers, as well as an estimate of the amounts payable under such agreements and arrangements as of the last day of fiscal 2024, see the &#8220;Severance and Change in Control Arrangements&#8221; section. </div><div id="toc869673_32" style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Severance and Separation Arrangements </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Any post-employment compensation payable to our Chief Executive Officer is governed solely by her employment agreement, the terms of which were the result of arms-length negotiations between her and the Compensation Committee. Under her employment agreement, Dr.&#160;Su is eligible to receive certain specified payments and benefits in the event that her employment is involuntarily terminated. The Compensation Committee believes that the amount payable to Dr.&#160;Su pursuant to her employment agreement is reasonable and competitive and provides transition assistance in the event of her involuntary termination of employment, with the goal of keeping her focused on our business rather than her personal circumstances. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">With the exception of our Chief Executive Officer and Mr.&#160;Peng, all of our other Named Executive Officers actively participate in our Executive Severance Plan for Executive and Senior Vice Presidents (the &#8220;Executive Severance Plan&#8221;). The Executive Severance Plan is designed to provide uniform treatment in the event of an involuntary termination of employment of our U.S. senior executives (except our Chief Executive Officer) and to provide transition assistance in such instances with the goal of keeping these senior executives focused on our business rather than their personal circumstances. A Named Executive Officer is not eligible to receive payments and benefits under the Executive Severance Plan if he or she receives severance payments and benefits in connection with a change of control of AMD pursuant to his or her change of control agreement. The Compensation Committee believes that the Executive Severance Plan provides the covered executives important protections and promotes our objectives of attracting and retaining executive talent. </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: arial; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="display:inline;">Payment by the Company of 12 months of COBRA premiums in the U.S., or similar benefit based on local norms for non-U.S. eligible executives. </div></div></td></tr></table><div id="toc869673_33" style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Other Compensation Policies </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Compensation Recovery (&#8220;Clawback&#8221;) Rights </div></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In November 2023, we adopted a compensation recovery (&#8220;clawback&#8221;) policy in compliance with the listing standards of Nasdaq. In the event that we are required to prepare an accounting restatement due to material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under U.S. securities law, the policy provides that we will recoup compensation from each current or former executive officer who, during the three-year period preceding the date on which a restatement is required, received compensation from incentive awards based on the erroneous financial data that exceeds the amount of incentive-based compensation the executive would have received based on the restatement. The Compensation Committee has sole discretion to determine how to seek recovery under the policy and may forgo recovery if it determines that recovery would be impracticable and either the cost of recovery would exceed the amount sought to be recovered, or that recovery would violate a home-country law that was adopted prior to November&#160;28, 2022, or would cause an otherwise <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">tax-qualified</div> retirement plan broadly available to our employees to fail to meet applicable tax qualification requirements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In addition, our Worldwide Standards of Business Conduct provide that we may pursue all remedies available under applicable law to recover any incentive-based or other compensation (including equity awards) paid or granted to our employees or agents in the event of such individual&#8217;s direct involvement with fraud, misconduct or gross negligence which contributes to an accounting restatement as a result of our material noncompliance with any financial reporting laws. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Finally, the award agreement for each stock option, RSU, and PRSU granted to an employee at or above the level of senior vice president (which includes our Named Executive Officers) includes a clawback provision. The clawback provides the Compensation Committee with the right to recover all or a portion of the compensation attributable to the award if the employee&#8217;s direct involvement with fraud, misconduct or his or her gross negligence contributes to or results in us being required to prepare an accounting restatement as a result of our material noncompliance with any financial reporting requirement under the federal<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"> </div></div>securities laws. The clawback does not apply to any award granted more than 18 months before the date of the first public issuance or SEC filing of the financial document embodying the reporting requirement. In addition, (a)&#160;with respect to awards granted in and after August 2015, we may recoup the award if the recipient violates the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-competition,</div> <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-solicitation</div> or confidentiality terms of the award agreement as permitted under applicable law, or fails to comply with any agreement with us regarding inventions, intellectual property rights, or proprietary information or material, and (b)&#160;with respect to awards granted after May 2019, we may recoup the award if the recipient engages in certain workplace misconduct (including sexual harassment or age, sex or other prohibited discrimination) or a criminal act involving moral turpitude. The Compensation Committee may exercise these clawback rights by cancellation, forfeiture, repayment or disgorgement of any profits realized by the employee from the sale of our securities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Stock Ownership Requirements </div></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Our stock ownership requirements are designed to increase our Named Executive Officers&#8217; stakes in us and to align their interests more closely with those of our stockholders. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">These requirements provide that on or before the Ownership Achievement Date (as defined below), our Chief Executive Officer should attain an investment position in our common stock equal to six times her then-current annual </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div>

Until the guideline is achieved, each Named Executive Officer is encouraged to retain at least 10% of the net shares obtained through our stock incentive plans. For this purpose, the &#8220;net shares&#8221; are the number of shares received from the exercise of stock options or the vesting of restricted stock or RSU awards, less the number of shares the Named Executive Officer sells to cover the exercise price of stock options or sells or has withheld to pay taxes. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">As of December&#160;28, 2024, each of our Named Executive Officers had satisfied his or her applicable stock ownership requirement or has time remaining to do so. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Deductibility of Executive Compensation </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">Section&#160;162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code (&#8220;Code&#8221;) generally disallows public companies a tax deduction for federal income tax purposes of remuneration in excess of $1&#160;million paid to certain executive officers. While the Compensation Committee may consider the deductibility of awards as one factor in determining our executive compensation, it also considers other factors in making its executive compensation decisions and retains the flexibility to grant awards or pay compensation the Compensation Committee determines to be consistent with its goals for our executive compensation program, even if the awards may not be deductible for tax purposes. </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:2.00pt solid #ffffff;vertical-align:top;background-color:#007298"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:arial;text-align:right"><span style="color:#FFFFFF">&#8194;2025 NOTICE OF MEETING AND PROXY STATEMENT&#8194;</span></p> <p style="font-size:3pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt;text-align:left">&#160;</p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center" id="toc869673_35">RISK ANALYSIS OF OUR COMPENSATION POLICIES AND PRACTICES </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In March 2025, the Compensation Committee reviewed our compensation policies and practices for employees generally and concluded that these policies and practices do not create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on us. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In reaching this conclusion, the Compensation Committee, with the assistance of management, assessed our executive and broad-based compensation and benefits programs to determine if any of them created undesired or excessive risks of a material nature. The assessment included (i)&#160;a review of our compensation policies and practices for employees generally, (ii)&#160;identification of the risks that could result from such policies and practices, (iii)&#160;identification of the risk mitigators and controls, and (iv)&#160;analysis of the potential risks against the risk mitigators and controls and our business strategy and objectives. Although the Compensation Committee reviewed our compensation programs, the Compensation Committee focused on the programs that have variability of payout and in which employees could directly affect the payout of incentives. These programs included the EIP, 2023 Annual Incentive Plan (&#8220;Annual Incentive Plan&#8221;), Long-Term Incentive Program (&#8220;LTI&#8221;), Sales Incentive Plan and 2023 Plan. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">In performing the assessment and reaching its conclusion, the Compensation Committee noted the following factors that the Compensation Committee believes may reduce the likelihood of undesired or excessive risk-taking: </p> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:5%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">Our overall compensation levels are competitive with the market; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:5%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">Our compensation practices and policies appropriately balance base pay versus variable pay and short-term versus long-term incentives; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:5%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">Although the EIP, Annual Incentive Plan, LTI and Sales Incentive Program have variability of payout, the Compensation Committee believes that any potential risks associated with such plans are controlled or mitigated by one or more of the following: (i)&#160;the performance goals being multi-dimensional (i.e., adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> net income, adjusted <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> free cash flow, revenue), thereby increasing the range of performance over which incentives are paid; (ii)&#160;the performance goals being aligned with our business objectives and being quantitative financial measures; (iii)&#160;the use of sliding payout scales, with the payouts in certain instances being linearly interpolated for performance falling between the performance levels set by the Compensation Committee; (iv)&#160;the ability of the Compensation Committee and/or management to exercise discretion to reduce payouts; (v)&#160;the existence of multiple internal controls and approval processes that are intended to prevent manipulation of outcomes by any employee, including the Named Executive Officers; and (vi)&#160;the incentive opportunities being capped; </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:5%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">Although the grant of equity awards under the 2023 Plan could motivate our employees to, among other things, focus on increasing our short-term stock price rather than the creation of long-term stockholder value, the Compensation Committee believes that potential risks are controlled or mitigated by one or more of the following: (i)&#160;awarding a combination of PRSUs, RSUs and stock options; (ii)&#160;three-year vesting and performance period for PRSUs (with the exception of the Value Creation Equity Awards granted in fiscal 2019, which have a five-year performance period); (iii)&#160;the vesting provisions of stock options and RSUs occurring over multi-year periods, (iv)&#160;caps on performance-based compensation opportunities; and (v)&#160;our stock ownership guidelines for our executive officers. In addition, we prohibit our employees, including Named Executive Officers, from engaging in hedging transactions in our securities; and </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:5%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:arial; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">We have implemented clawback provisions and policies, as described in more detail in &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8221; above. </p></td></tr></table>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

The grant date fair value (which is sometimes referred to herein as the &#8220;accounting value&#8221;) is used to recognize the accounting expense for long-term equity awards. For fiscal 2024, the amounts shown include the grant date fair value of the PRSUs awarded in fiscal 2024 to each Named Executive Officer other than Mr.&#160;Peng, as set forth in the table below. The grant date fair value of the PRSUs is calculated by an outside professional valuation consultant using a Monte-Carlo simulation model and based upon a discounted cash flow analysis of the probability-weighted payoffs of a share-based payment assuming a variety of possible stock price paths and represents the estimate of the most probable aggregate compensation cost to be recognized over the requisite service period determined as of the grant date under ASC Topic 718. There were no stock awards to Mr.&#160;Peng during fiscal 2024. The amount reported for Mr.&#160;Peng for fiscal 2024 represents the incremental fair value, determined in accordance with ASC Topic 718, associated with (i)&#160;vesting service credit with respect to his outstanding unvested RSUs as of his retirement and <span style="white-space:nowrap">(ii)&#160;pro-rated</span> vesting at target-level performance for Mr.&#160;Peng&#8217;s 2022 PRSUs based on completed service during the applicable performance period, in each case pursuant to the terms of his Retirement Transition Agreement. For a discussion of the assumptions made in the valuations reflected in this column, see Note 12 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in our Annual Report. For more information on the RSUs and PRSUs held by Mr.&#160;Peng during fiscal 2024, see &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8212;Retirement Transition Agreement&#8221; above. </p></td></tr></table>

<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(6)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">For Dr.&#160;Su, the amount reflects (a)&#160;aggregate incremental costs for personal security services in the total amount of $14,862 and (b) $24,147 in personal expenses for guests in connection with business-related travel where the presence of spouses/partners was requested by us. We do not consider security expenses for Dr.&#160;Su to be personal benefits, rather an appropriate expense for our benefit. For more information, see &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8212;Fiscal 2024 Compensation Elements&#8212;Health, Welfare, Security and Other Personal Benefits (Perquisites)&#8221; above. For Mr. Papermaster, the amount reflects (a) a filing fee under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvement Act of 1976, as amended (&#8220;HSR&#8221;), in the amount of $105,000, which was paid by AMD on behalf of Mr. Papermaster and (b) $12,497 for the direct cost of a commercial airline flight and other personal expenses for a guest in connection with business-related travel where the presence of spouses/partners was requested by us. No tax gross-up was provided to Mr. Papermaster for the HSR fee. See additional detail under the section entitled &#8220;Health, Welfare, Security and Other Personal Benefits (Perquisites). For Mr.&#160;Norrod, the amount reflects the direct costs of commercial airline flights and other personal expenses for guests in connection with business-related travel where the presence of spouses/partners was requested by us. For Mr.&#160;Peng, the amount reflects the total COBRA reimbursement benefit provided by the Company pursuant to the terms of his Retirement Transition Agreements in fiscal 2024. </p></td></tr></table>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Amounts reflect the grant date fair value of the respective award computed in accordance with ASC Topic 718. With respect to the PRSUs, in accordance with SEC rules, amounts reflect the fair value at the grant date determined using a Monte-Carlo simulation model and based upon a discounted cash flow analysis of the probability-weighted payoffs of a share-based payment assuming a variety of possible stock price paths and represents the estimate of aggregate compensation cost to be recognized over the requisite service period determined as of the grant date under ASC Topic 718. For Mr.&#160;Peng, the amount reflects the incremental fair value, determined in accordance with ASC Topic 718, associated with the (i)&#160;acceleration of 28,841 RSUs for $3,992,748, (ii) extension of the exercise period of his outstanding vested stock options for $332,998 and <span style="white-space:nowrap">(iii)&#160;pro-rated</span> vesting at target for his 2022 PRSUs for $4,958,921 based on completed service during applicable performance periods, in each case pursuant to the terms of his Retirement Transition Agreement with the Company. For a discussion of the assumptions made in the valuations reflected in this column, see Note 12 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in our Annual Report. For more information on the stock options, RSUs and PRSUs held by Mr.&#160;Peng during fiscal 2024, see &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8212;Retirement Transition Agreement&#8221; above. </p></td></tr></table>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(6)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">There were no stock option or stock awards granted to Mr.&#160;Peng during fiscal 2024. The amounts reflect (a)&#160;the number of shares issued to Mr.&#160;Peng during fiscal 2024 in settlement of the PRSUs and RSUs that vested upon termination and (b)&#160;the number of stock options that vested upon termination pursuant to his Retirement Transition Agreement. </p></td></tr></table>

These amounts do not represent above-market or preferential earnings (within the meaning of 17 CFR Section&#160;229.402(c)(2)(viii)), and as a result are not reported in the &#8220;2024 Summary Compensation Table&#8221; above. </p></td></tr></table>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(3)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:arial;text-align:left">Other than executive contributions in the fiscal year, no other aggregate amounts were reported as compensation for the Named Executive Officers in 2024, 2023 and 2022. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">We maintain the DIA, which allows eligible employees, including the Named Executive Officers, to voluntarily defer receipt of a portion of their salary, bonus and any commission payments until the date or dates selected by the participant. Participants may defer up to 50% of annual base salary and/or 100% of commissions and bonuses. Earnings on the deferred accounts are based on the performance of the investment funds selected by the participants. Participants make a deferral election, prior to the year in which the compensation is earned, that may not be terminated or changed during the year for which it was made. Generally, we make a discretionary contribution to the participant&#8217;s account if his or her annual base salary, minus his or her Section&#160;401(k) contribution before the deferral, is greater than the annual compensation limit for Section&#160;401(k) plans. The contribution, if any, is equal to the lesser of (i)&#160;50% of the deferred compensation credited to the participant&#8217;s account for the year or (ii)&#160;a discretionary percentage of the participant&#8217;s base salary in excess of the eligible Section&#160;401(k) compensation limit for the year minus the participant&#8217;s Section&#160;401(k) contributions. For 2024, our discretionary contribution percentage under option (ii)&#160;above was 4.5%. Participants are 100% vested in the value of their accounts. Participants may select their desired benchmark investment fund(s) in which their accounts are deemed to be invested and may change their investment elections at any time, with such change effective as of the next business day. The amount of investment gain or loss that is credited to the participant&#8217;s account depends on the participant&#8217;s investment election. For 2024, we utilized investment funds in an array of asset classes, substantially aligned to those offered under our Section&#160;401(k) plan. We have placed assets in mutual funds held in a Rabbi trust established for the DIA. For 2024, the investment return credited to Dr.&#160;Su&#8217;s, Ms.&#160;Hu&#8217;s, and Mr.&#160;Papermaster&#8217;s DIA accounts was 10.7%, 15.8% and 8.8%, respectively, based on their investment elections for their respective DIA accounts. This investment return was calculated by taking the aggregate gain or loss in fiscal 2024 and dividing it by the aggregate balance as of the beginning of fiscal 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">The DIA accounts are distributed following a participant&#8217;s termination of employment with us unless the participant has elected an <span style="white-space:nowrap">in-service</span> withdrawal (scheduled or hardship withdrawal). At the time a participant makes his or her deferral election, he or she may elect a different form of distribution for such year&#8217;s deferred compensation. The participant may elect a single lump sum distribution or annual installment distributions over three to ten years. The default form of distribution is a single lump sum. A participant may change the form of distribution election, subject to the terms of the DIA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:5%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial">A participant may elect to withdraw all or part of his or her account while employed by us, subject to the terms of the DIA. The <span style="white-space:nowrap">in-service</span> withdrawal date must be at least two years after the plan year in which the election was made. An <span style="white-space:nowrap">in-service</span> withdrawal date may be changed, subject to the terms of the DIA. An unscheduled payment may also be made, subject to the terms of the DIA. </p>
